dct_description_sm:
This dataset comprises output from reforestation and net-zero CO2 pathway simulations run using the University of Victoria Earth System Climate Model, version 2.10 and is compliment to the forthcoming article to be published in Communications Earth & Environment, the pre-print and detailed description of which is available here: https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-6355003/v1

We investigated whether using reforestation-based CO2 removal to offset fossil fuel CO2 emissions will lead to the same climate outcome as avoiding additional fossil fuel CO2 emissions. This net-zero case was derived by accounting for reforestation-based CO2 removals from reforestation simulations, then placing these removals as additional fossil fuel CO2 emissions on top of a reference emissions pathway. The resulting 'net-zero pathway' was compared to reference case. Our results, as found in this dataset, show that the net-zero pathways leads to carbon and climate imbalance compared to the reference case. The biogeophysical effects of reforestation and potential re-release of removed carbon through disturbance events amplifies the additional warming found in our net-zero simulations. 

Please see the UVic-ESCM 2.10 model description paper for additional information:

Mengis N., Keller D.P., MacDougall A.H., Eby M., Wright N., Meissner K.J., Oschlies A., Schmittner A., MacIsaac A.J., Matthews H.D., & Zickfeld K. (2020). Evaluation of the University of Victoria Earth System Climate Model version 2.10 (UVic ESCM 2.10). Geosci. Model Dev., 13, 4183–4204. https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-13-4183-2020
